_description: Cross-layer test vectors for driver version verdict. All three layers (Python, bash, PowerShell) must produce identical verdicts for each vector. R-01 (v0.19.0): malformed/sentinel inputs are included deliberately -- the bash layer previously graded every non-numeric-leading string as PASS while Python returned WARN, and a well-formed-only vector set let that cross-layer divergence pass CI.
_expected_reason_description:
OPTIONAL per-vector key, asserted by all three harnesses ONLY when present. It pins DRIVER_VERDICT_REASON (bash), $script:StreamDriverVerdictReason (PowerShell) and details['verdict_reason'] (Python) -- the channel each layer uses to distinguish WHY a verdict was reached, where the verdict string alone is ambiguous.

Two reasons carry real consequences and are therefore tagged here:
  at_stream_max      -- F-03. Routes the finding to the weight-0 `platform` domain (bash gate 22 / Python BSOD_PLATFORM_DRIVER_STREAM_CAPPED) instead of `driver`, because on a capped stream it is the only reachable verdict and no VM-level action can clear it.
  below_tooling_floor -- F-06. Makes Gate 15 cite KCS-7128506 (a collection UTILITY article, excluded from kcs_trigger_articles) rather than KCS-7141291, which is the difference between GENERAL-KNOWLEDGE (3.15) and KCS-VALIDATED (4.50). bash and Python disagreed on exactly this for a long time and the gate-keyed risk-tier vectors could not see it.

The remaining reasons (empty_version, unparseable_version, binary_format_version) are deliberately NOT tagged yet: bash distinguishes empty_version from unparseable_version while Python conflates both into one WARN, so a complete back-fill needs that reconciled first.

_os_compat_vectors_description: N-06 (Wave 7, R-47): a SEPARATE axis from `vectors` above -- evaluate_guest_os_driver_compatibility (bash) / Get-GuestOSDriverCompatibility (PowerShell) / check_virtio_win_os_compatibility (Python), all consuming shared/virtio-win-guest-os-support.json. Keyed by (os_hint, driver_version) rather than (version, stream) because this axis has no host-stream concept at all -- deliberately a new key in this same file rather than retrofitting `vectors`' schema, which the three existing harnesses already consume in a form with no os_hint field. Every INCOMPATIBLE expectation below is now grounded in KCS 4234591 ('Certified Guest Operating Systems in OpenShift Virtualization') rather than driver-archaeology inference alone -- see shared/virtio-win-guest-os-support.json's _kcs_4234591 field.

os_compat_vectors.note: XP: KCS 4234591 'Known to work' tier + EOL footnote (not Certified) -- fires regardless of the specific (even a current, otherwise-PASS) version reported
'winxp' substring match within a longer free-form os_hint string, and fires even with NO driver version evidence at all -- the incompatibility is intrinsic to the OS, not the reported number
Server 2003: KCS 4234591 'Known to work' tier + EOL footnote
Server 2008 (and R2): KCS 4234591 'Known to work' tier + EOL footnote

Server 2012 (and R2): KCS 4234591 'Known to work' tier + EOL footnote -- fires even though the article notes 2012 R2 has MTV Status 'Blue' (migrated VMs run), since 'runs' is not the same as 'Certified/supported'

Windows 7: KCS 4234591 'Known to work' tier + EOL footnote settles this independently of the driver-version ceiling this file could not establish on its own (superseded the earlier CEILING_NOT_YET_ESTABLISHED placeholder) -- fires even for a version that would otherwise PASS on the ordinary stream axis
Windows 8: absent from ALL FOUR of KCS 4234591's support tiers (weaker than even 'Known to work') -- fires even at the current remediation baseline version

Windows 8.1: same as win8 -- absent from KCS 4234591 entirely; also proves win81 is matched distinctly from win8 (both contain the substring 'win8'), not swallowed by win8's negative-lookahead pattern

Windows 10: still Certified per KCS 4234591 as of this writing (even though Microsoft's own consumer support lapsed 2025-10-14 -- see the shared JSON's _known_gaps) -- must not fire regardless of driver version (this axis defers to Red Hat's own certification matrix, not Microsoft's lifecycle dates, for currently-Certified OSes)
Windows Server 2022: Certified per KCS 4234591 -- must not fire even for a driver version far below any stream threshold (that is check_virtio_win_version's job, not this axis's)
empty os_hint -- unknown/uncollected OS metadata must not fire this check (fail-silent, not fail-open into a false INCOMPATIBLE)

Win32_OperatingSystem.Caption long-form string (collect-windows-guest-info.ps1's guest-local input, distinct from the terse cluster-side os_hint convention above) -- must match the same as the terse 'winxp' token per _match_pattern_inputs
Caption long-form with interposed '(R)' trademark symbols (a real quirk of legacy Windows Server 2003/XP-era Captions) -- proves the bounded '.{0,N}' filler in match_pattern tolerates it
Caption long-form, Server 2008 R2 (no trademark symbols in this Caption vintage)
Caption long-form, Server 2012 R2
Caption long-form, Windows 7 -- proves 'windows\s?7(?!\d)' matches the space-separated Caption form, not just the terse 'win7' token
Caption long-form, Windows 8
Caption long-form, Windows 8.1 -- proves 'windows\s?8\.1' is matched distinctly from plain 'windows\s?8', mirroring the terse win8/win81 disambiguation
Caption long-form, Windows 10 (Certified) -- must not fire, and must not be swallowed by the win7/win8 Caption patterns (e.g. 'Windows 10' contains neither ' 7' nor ' 8' immediately after 'Windows')
Caption long-form, Server 2022 (Certified) -- must not fire and must not false-positive against the 2003/2008/2012 Caption patterns
